chunks: The number of his students reached three hundred mujtahids from the Shia (al-Khāṣṣa), and from the Sunni (al-ʿĀmma) their number cannot be counted.

key_terms.الْخَاصَّةِ: al-Khāṣṣa — the Shia; classical term for the followers of the Imams
key_terms.الْعَامَّةِ: al-ʿĀmma — the Sunni; classical term for the general Muslim public
key_terms.مُجْتَهِدٍ: mujtahid — a scholar qualified to derive independent legal rulings through ijtihad

ai.seo_question: How many students did Shaykh al-Ṭūsī (Shaykh al-Ṭāʾifa) have from both the Shia and Sunni communities?
ai.summary: This biographical note records the extraordinary scholarly reach of Shaykh al-Ṭāʾifa Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī (385–460 AH), the compiler of Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām. It attests that he produced three hundred mujtahid-level students from the Shia community, while his Sunni students were so numerous as to be uncountable — a testament to his unparalleled stature in the Islamic scholarly world of fifth-century Baghdad. The classical terms al-Khāṣṣa (the particular ones) and al-ʿĀmma (the general public) were standard designations in Shia scholarly literature for the Shia and Sunni communities respectively.
word_analysis: the Shia (the particular/elite followers of the Imams)
